title: POC Weekly Sync - Quantization (INT8/FP8)
summary: Weekly POC sync to review INT8/FP8 quantization experiment results. Redwood presented perf deltas and quality regressions (small) on priority evals; customer requested extended eval on customer prompts, clarified latency SLOs and KV cache behavior, and agreed next steps: share benchmark spreadsheet, run extended 5k prompt eval, schedule on-prem latency test.
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-04-14
Time: 10:00 AM UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen, Ethan Park, Jordan Li (Redwood); Lara Nguyen, Carlos Martinez, Priya Shah, Samir Patel (Acme Financial)

Summary (auto): quick review of int8/fp8 runs, perf numbers, a few quality diffs, next steps to share artifacts

00:00 Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, uh we'll kick off, i think we have 45 minutes, please flag if anyone needs more time
00:15 Lara Nguyen: thanks maya, yep all good on time here, excited to see the numbers
00:28 Ethan Park: ok quick agenda, recap of last week's runs, INT8 vs FP8 perf deltas, quality impact on your eval set, and actions; jordan will drop the spreadsheet link afterwards
00:45 Carlos Martinez: quick note, we're mainly focused on 99th percentile token latency for inference, plus tail latency under burst, and also cost per 1M tokens
01:10 Maya Chen: perfect, that's what we tuned for; ethan, you wanna run the perf slide?
01:22 Ethan Park: yeah, so baseline is fp16 model on our Dedicated pool, average token latency at 1k batch was ~8ms, throughput X, cost baseline Y. INT8 runs showed 20-25% throughput improvement and 15-20% lower cost, FP8 was slightly better for throughput we're seeing about 30% throughput up from fp16 on same infra.
01:58 Lara Nguyen: quick clar, the "fp8" you're referring to is the experimental e4 profile right? it had some kernel fusion enabled?
02:10 Ethan Park: correct, fp8-e4 with kernel_fuse on, and we used calibration from a 10k sample. calibration matters, we saw variance if calibration set wasn't representative
02:35 Priya Shah: any obvious quality regressions to flag?
02:45 Ethan Park: overall on out-of-box benchmarks, quality drop from FP16->INT8 is small, like median delta <0.5% on our rouge/accuracy heuristics, FP8 even smaller. but we observed specific prompt patterns where INT8 introduces hallucination risk on chain-of-thought long sequences.
03:15 Lara Nguyen: can you give an example?
03:22 Ethan Park: sure, we have an example in the spreadsheet, but to paraphrase: multi-step financial reconciliation prompts with long KV cache usage tended to drift for int8. FP8 held up better.
03:40 Samir Patel: is that likely due to kv cache quantization noise?
03:50 Ethan Park: yeah our suspicion is kv cache accumulation with lower precision causes small numerical drift in attention scores; we mitigated some by increasing attention softmax stability thresholds and tweaking kv cache flushing frequency in the runtime
04:20 Carlos Martinez: how big was the delta in token-level probabilities? like is it a catastrophic switch or small probability mass shift?
04:32 Ethan Park: mostly small shifts  probability mass reallocation of ~1-3% on the token distribution, except on the failure cases where the top-1 changed and that yielded the hallucinated token
05:05 Lara Nguyen: hmm okay, that's actionable. our eval set has a lot of long-form prompts, so we care about that tail behaviour
05:20 Maya Chen: to be explicit, our recommendation for now: FP8 for long-form customer workloads; INT8 for short-to-medium prompts where cost is a priority and latency is key. we can also do hybrid routing: route long-form to fp8 variants, short to int8.
05:45 Priya Shah: hybrid routing sounds nice, do you support automatic routing by length or by model score?
05:55 Ethan Park: yes we have policy-based routing in the platform you can pick by prompt length, estimated tokens, or an eval classifier to decide. we can help set that up in your test env
06:20 Jordan Li: dropping the bench link now (note: link short, public docs), spreadsheet has token-level traces, discrepancy examples, and perf numbers per instance type
06:38 Lara Nguyen: got it, i'll look after the call
07:00 Maya Chen: next i want to talk about the 99th pctl tail: we ran burst tests simulating your traffic pattern, fp8 kept tail within 1.3x baseline while int8 had larger variance at high concurrency, probably due to different kernel scheduling
07:28 Samir Patel: does that correlate with GPU memory pressure? our infra often hits memory churn during spikes
07:40 Ethan Park: partly. INT8 reduced memory footprint so we could pack more, but under raid-batching the scheduling leads to contention that can raise tail latency this is tunable (batching window, continuous batching policy)
08:05 Carlos Martinez: any recommended config changes for our Dedicated pool?
08:12 Maya Chen: yes, we suggest: smaller max_batch for INT8 lanes, increase batching timeout slightly for fp8 lanes, enable prefix KV caching for recurrent prompts to reduce recompute, and set autoscaler to keep buffer GPU headroom at ~15% under expected peak
08:38 Lara Nguyen: TTL on KV cache any tradeoffs? we want cache to reduce cost but not staleness
08:48 Ethan Park: we typically set KV cache TTL based on prompt variation; for stable conversation flows, longer TTL is good. for financial reconciliation sequences, we flush per session at end to avoid leakage.
09:12 Priya Shah: security question are the token-level traces redacted? any PII risk in the traces you shared?
09:22 Jordan Li: good call; the spreadsheet we shared is sanitized with placeholder tokens, but we can provide raw traces under NDA and in a private S3 with KMS if needed
09:40 Lara Nguyen: we'll sign NDA if needed, probably want raw traces to run our evals
09:48 Maya Chen: we'll initiate the NDA process, and we can also provide a private bucket link with KMS access for your team
10:10 Carlos Martinez: on the regression detection side, how do you flag quality regressions during a rollout?
10:20 Ethan Park: our rollout pipeline runs regression evals on your golden prompts and can auto-block a rollout if defined thresholds exceed. we also surface token-level diffs and classification of regression types (hallucination, truncation, formatting)
10:45 Lara Nguyen: nice, is that part of Redwood Optimize or Console?
10:52 Maya Chen: it's integrated rollouts + Optimize + Console dashboards. we can give you a demo of the gating rules
11:12 Priya Shah: ok back to perf numbers can you summarize cost delta again for a 1M token workload under our mix?
11:25 Ethan Park: rough: INT8 is ~18% cheaper vs FP16; FP8 ~22% cheaper; depending on batch shapes it varies. in your traffic mix (mix of short+long) hybrid routing gave us a 15-20% cost improvement with negligible customer-visible latency changes
12:00 Samir Patel: what's the max batch size you tested on our Dedicated config?
12:10 Ethan Park: we tested up to batch 2k tokens on the same GPU setup you provisioned, but we recommend starting with conservative batch of 512 for int8 lane and 1024 for fp8 if tail is a concern
12:38 Lara Nguyen: any surprising edge cases you found?
12:45 Ethan Park: yes one: some tokenizers with bpe variants produced slightly different token splits which amplified quantization noise; we patched tokenizer normalization to be consistent across pipelines
13:05 Maya Chen: action item for us to share tokenizer normalization patch notes
13:12 Ethan Park: i'll add that in the spreadsheet notes
13:20 Lara Nguyen: sounds good
13:30 Maya Chen: ok let's go over the evaluation plan customer side  lar a?
13:36 Lara Nguyen: we want to run an extended eval: 5k representative prompts, compare fp16/int8/fp8, look at top-1 diffs, rouge, and a small human review set for hallucinations; we'd also like latency histograms and cost breakdowns
14:00 Ethan Park: perfect. we can provide tooling to run those locally against your private deployment or run them in our dedicated test environment. for raw traces we'll need NDA+S3 creds.
14:22 Priya Shah: timeline how long to get results if we give you prompts by end of next week?
14:30 Maya Chen: if prompts are provided by Apr 17, we can return a full report by Apr 23 (6 business days), including examples and recommended configs
14:50 Carlos Martinez: can you also include a canary rollout recipe? we want step-by-step to move from fp16 to hybrid lanes without user impact
15:02 Ethan Park: sure, we have runbooks will attach to the spreadsheet; includes gating thresholds, traffic weights, and rollback triggers
15:20 Jordan Li: adding runbook link to notes
15:30 Lara Nguyen: on-prem test we want one latency-run on our on-prem hardware next week, can Redwood help with agent install?
15:40 Maya Chen: yes, our private deployment team can remote assist; ethan will coordinate agent config and scheduling
16:00 Ethan Park: note for on-prem run we recommend disabling aggressive quantization fusion initially, and run fp16 then fp8 then int8, capture token-level deltas
16:22 Samir Patel: we'll provision a test node and share SSH jumpbox creds under NDA
16:30 Priya Shah: ok, security checklist SOC2, KMS, audit logs, SSO: we saw the docs but may need deeper answers for encryption-at-rest for traces
16:44 Maya Chen: we will resend the security pack with details on encryption, RBAC, and audit logs. for traces we can store in customer-owned bucket with KMS and provide access logs
17:05 Lara Nguyen: great
17:15 Maya Chen: any blocker from your side on the proposed evaluation plan?
17:22 Lara Nguyen: no blockers, just internal schedule alignment to collect prompts
17:30 Carlos Martinez: one more question, what about mixed-precision fallback during spikes? if int8 lane is overloaded can it automatically fallback to fp8 or fp16 to preserve latency?
17:44 Ethan Park: yes, policy-based fallback exists we can configure overflow fallback to fp8 or fp16 by capacity tier; it's how we ensure graceful degradation
18:05 Priya Shah: cool, helps with reliability SLA
18:12 Maya Chen: ok let's go over explicit next steps and owners
18:20 (brief pause)
18:30 Maya Chen: i'll read them out: Maya to share benchmark spreadsheet + token traces in sanitized form and initiate NDA; Ethan to run extra decoder regression and attach examples; Acme (Lara) to provide 5k prompts and latency SLOs; Samir to provision on-prem test node and creds. agreed?
18:55 Lara Nguyen: agreed
19:05 Carlos Martinez: agreed
19:12 Priya Shah: agreed
19:20 Maya Chen: great, i'll also schedule the on-prem run for next Tue-Wed tentative
19:30 Jordan Li: dropping links to runbook, security pack, and spreadsheet (see notes)
19:45 Maya Chen: thanks everyone, any final quick comments?
19:52 Lara Nguyen: no, thanks team talk soon
20:00 End of recording
